questions.question: 1. Which of the following statements specifies velocity?
options: b. Displacement made per unit time
c. Acceleration in a given time
d. Deceleration in a given time
questions.answer_guide: Velocity = displacement per unit time (a vector).

questions.question: 2. What is the average velocity of a car which shows down uniform from 30m/s
questions.answer_guide: The question is incomplete as printed (no final velocity is given). For uniform deceleration, average velocity = (u + v)/2. If the car stops (v = 0) the answer is 15 m/s, which is not an option; if it slows to 10 m/s the answer is 20 m/s (b).

questions.question: 3. A bullet of mass 5g is fired from a gun of mass 500g at a speed of 400 m/s. Calculate the recoiling speed of the gun.
questions.answer_guide: Conservation of momentum: 0.005 × 400 = 0.5 × v → v = 4 m/s

questions.question: 4. The figure shows the forces acting on wooden block. If the block accelerates at 2 m/s², calculate the mass of the block.

questions.question: 13. An electric power is transmitted along cables of resistance 5Ω with the current of 1.2 A workout the power loss in the line (P=I²R).
14. A transformer is a device used to
options: b. Chance AC from one value to another
c. Increase the energy of AC voltage
d. Smooth the value of AC voltage
questions.answer_guide: A transformer changes (steps up or down) an AC voltage from one value to another.

questions.question: 15. If the same mass of sand and water are heated in the same way, the sand heats up quicker than water. This is because:
options: a. Sand is a solid and water is a liquid
b. Sand has less specific heat capacity than water
c. Sand has higher specific heat capacity than water
d. Sand has more density than water.
questions.answer_guide: Lower specific heat capacity → less energy needed per °C → heats up faster.

questions.question: 16. Volume of a fixed mass of gas at constant pressure is directly proportional to the temperature. This law is known as:
questions.answer_guide: V ∝ T at constant pressure – Charles' law.

questions.question: 17. Which of the following components is an example of intrinsic semi-conductor.
questions.answer_guide: An LDR is made from a pure (undoped) semiconductor such as cadmium sulphide, whose resistance falls with light; diodes, LEDs and transistors use doped (extrinsic) p-n junctions.

questions.question: 18. Which of the components is used for safety purpose.
questions.answer_guide: A circuit breaker cuts off the current when it becomes too large.

questions.answer_guide:
a. Maximum velocity ≈ 20 m/s
b. ii. Uniform acceleration (the graph is a straight line sloping upwards).
c. Distance = area under the graph = ½ × base × height. Reading 20 m/s at about 3 s: distance = ½ × 3 × 20 = 30 m. Average velocity = (0 + 20)/2 = 10 m/s (or 30 m ÷ 3 s = 10 m/s).
   (The printed graph is not drawn exactly to scale; if 20 m/s is taken at 4 s, distance = 40 m and the average velocity is still 10 m/s.)

questions.question:
2. The figure below shows a force against extension graph for a spring. The spring obeys Hooker's law.
  a. State Hooker's law in words (2marks)
  b. From the graph, find out the spring constant in N/cm. (2marks)
  c. On the graph mark X, to identify the elastic limit of the spring. (2marks)

diagram.caption: Force-extension graph: a straight line from the origin to about 8 N at 5 cm, after which the line curves and levels off near 10 N.

questions.answer_guide:
a. The extension of a spring is directly proportional to the force (load) applied to it, provided the elastic limit is not exceeded.
b. k = F/e from the straight part of the graph ≈ 8 N ÷ 5 cm = 1.6 N/cm
c. X is marked at the point where the straight line begins to curve – at about 5 cm extension (≈ 8 N).

questions.question:
6.
  a. Define nuclear fission? (2marks)
  b. Use words below to identify the following nuclear reactions, Fission, Fusion, Normal reaction. (3marks)
     ¹₁H + ⁷₃Li → 2(⁴₂He) → ........
     ²³⁵₉₂U + ¹₀n → ¹⁴⁰₅₄Xe + ⁹⁴₃₈Sr + 2(¹₀n) → ........
     ²₁H + ³₁H → ⁴₂He + ¹₀n → ........
  c. Identify one advantage of nuclear fission? (1mark)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus (e.g. uranium-235) into two lighter nuclei when it absorbs a neutron, releasing a large amount of energy and more neutrons.
b. ¹₁H + ⁷₃Li → 2⁴₂He: Normal reaction (artificial transmutation)
   ²³⁵₉₂U + ¹₀n → ¹⁴⁰₅₄Xe + ⁹⁴₃₈Sr + 2¹₀n: Fission
   ²₁H + ³₁H → ⁴₂He + ¹₀n: Fusion
c. Any one: releases a very large amount of energy from a small mass of fuel; produces no greenhouse gases (CO₂) when generating electricity.

questions.question:
8. In the equation Q = mL_F
  a. The letter L_F stands for specific latent heat of fusion, describe what is meant by specific latent heat of fusion? (2marks)
  b. Explain why a piece of ice placed in water cools it down. (2marks)
  c. Calculate the quantity of heat needed to melt 20g of ice at 0⁰C into water at same temperature (L_F = 340 J/g) (2marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Specific latent heat of fusion is the quantity of heat needed to change 1 kg (or 1 g) of a solid into liquid at its melting point without any change in temperature.
b. The ice absorbs heat (latent heat of fusion) from the water in order to melt, and the cold melted water also absorbs heat as it warms up; the water loses this heat, so its temperature falls.
c. Q = mL_F = 20 × 340 = 6800 J (6.8 kJ)

questions.question:
10. Friction is the force that opposes the motion of an object when the objects slide over each other.
  a. State one advantage and one disadvantage of friction in real life? (2marks)
  b. Suggest one way to increase friction between two surfaces. (2marks)
  c. What is the name given to specific friction in air? (2marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Advantage (any one): allows us to walk without slipping; makes brakes work; lets tyres grip the road; lets us hold objects or strike a match.
   Disadvantage (any one): causes wear and tear of machine parts; wastes energy as heat; reduces efficiency of machines.
b. Any one: make the surfaces rougher (e.g. treads on tyres, sand on roads); increase the force pressing the surfaces together.
c. Air resistance (drag).
